title: Anime Head Construction: Comprehensive Capstone and Self-Review
summary: Plan, construct, vary, light, critique, revise, and present one identity-consistent anime head model sheet using the complete beginner workflow, with explicit evidence and artist-controlled completion.
learning_objectives: Translate a short character and lighting brief into measurable construction decisions.
Produce front and three-quarter identity-consistent heads plus one expression variation.
Apply controlled asymmetry and cel-value grouping without losing structural anchors.
Use tutor evidence as suggestions requiring explicit acceptance or rejection.
Revise from prioritized causes rather than polishing every symptom.
Complete a final self-review and delayed-repetition plan without automatic grading.

theory.title: A capstone integrates decisions
theory.explanation: The final exercise is not a speed test or a request for perfection. It demonstrates that construction, identity, expression, asymmetry, perspective, and lighting decisions can coexist and remain explainable.

theory.title: Briefs constrain useful choices
theory.explanation: A short brief names character tendency, identity anchors, expression, view, and light. Constraints reduce random iteration and make review evidence relevant to an intended outcome.

theory.title: Review should prioritize causes
theory.explanation: Cranial volume, orientation, identity anchors, and major value grouping affect many downstream details. Correct high-leverage causes before eyelash, fold, edge, or rendering polish.

theory.title: Revision history is evidence of learning
theory.explanation: Retain the initial attempt and accepted/rejected tutor previews according to project settings. A correction note should state what changed, why, and whether the next attempt improved the intended relationship.

theory.title: Completion remains the artist's decision
theory.explanation: Rubric scores and tutor suggestions support judgement but never auto-complete the project. Completion means the checklist is satisfied, unresolved limitations are named, and a specific delayed practice target is chosen.

steps.title: 1. Write the brief and identity card
steps.explanation: Name the character tendency, five-to-eight identity anchors, one controlled asymmetry, one expression, and one light statement. Mark which choices are fixed and which may vary.

steps.title: 2. Construct the front control
steps.explanation: Build cranium, jaw, axes, eyes, muzzle/nose, mouth, and ears before decoration. Check proportions against the identity card and correct accidental asymmetry.

steps.title: 3. Construct the three-quarter identity view
steps.explanation: Rebuild forms in depth, preserve anchors, separate perspective compression from design asymmetry, and verify nose, mouth, ear, and jaw attachment.

steps.title: 4. Add the expression variation
steps.explanation: Apply the named expression through coordinated lids, brows, cheeks, and mouth while holding persistent identity and structural anchors stable.

steps.title: 5. Design two-value lighting
steps.explanation: Declare the light, map planes, create flat light/shadow families, and label form versus cast causes in both views.

steps.title: 6. Request and triage reviews
steps.explanation: Place manual landmarks on the relevant layers, inspect raw and normalized evidence, and rank corrections by structural leverage. Accept or reject every preview explicitly.

steps.title: 7. Produce the correction pass
steps.explanation: Revise cranial/orientation causes first, identity/feature relationships second, expression/asymmetry third, and value grouping fourth. Record one sentence per accepted change.

steps.title: 8. Compare before and after
steps.explanation: Use compatible metrics and visual overlays without ranking yourself globally. Identify improved, unchanged, and declined dimensions and distinguish measurement limitations from drawing limitations.

steps.title: 9. Finalize and plan repetition
steps.explanation: Complete the checklist manually, name unresolved limitations, export the model sheet, and schedule one focused repeat after a delay without tracing the final result.

guided_drills.title: Brief-to-thumbnail
guided_drills.instructions: Write three different five-line briefs and produce a small front/turned construction pair for each before selecting one capstone.

guided_drills.title: Correction prioritization
guided_drills.instructions: Given five observed symptoms, rank the likely structural causes and explain which single correction has the largest downstream effect.

guided_drills.title: Accept/reject rationale
guided_drills.instructions: For five tutor guides, write one sentence accepting, rejecting, or deferring the suggestion using the brief and visible evidence.

guided_drills.title: Delayed reconstruction
guided_drills.instructions: Reconstruct the selected character from its identity card after a delay, once in front and once turned, without viewing the final artwork.

common_mistakes.symptom: The capstone becomes an endless polish project.
common_mistakes.cause: No brief, checklist, or stopping condition was declared.
common_mistakes.correction: Return to the measurable brief and defer decoration unrelated to its learning targets.

common_mistakes.symptom: Every tutor suggestion is accepted automatically.
common_mistakes.cause: Scores were treated as authority rather than provisional evidence.
common_mistakes.correction: Compare each guide with the brief, construction, and explanation; reject unsupported advice explicitly.

common_mistakes.symptom: Details are revised while the cranium is wrong.
common_mistakes.cause: Symptoms were prioritized over high-leverage structural causes.
common_mistakes.correction: Correct volume and orientation first, then identity, features, expression, and values.
Rebuild from the identity card and label perspective-only changes.

common_mistakes.symptom: Expression or asymmetry moves unrelated anchors.
common_mistakes.cause: One side of the whole head was shifted.
common_mistakes.correction: Restore stable construction and isolate only the named temporary or persistent difference.

common_mistakes.cause: Dark shapes were used to cover unresolved features.
common_mistakes.correction: Review the unshaded construction, then rebuild the value mask from explicit planes.

common_mistakes.symptom: Completion is inferred from a score.
common_mistakes.correction: Use the manual checklist, name limitations, and choose the next delayed exercise yourself.

completion_criteria: The brief, identity card, asymmetry intent, expression, and light statement are explicit.
Front and three-quarter construction views preserve identity anchors.
Expression and controlled asymmetry change only intended relationships.
Two-value lighting is coherent across views and major boundaries have causes.
Tutor evidence was reviewed and every preview explicitly accepted or rejected.
The correction pass records what changed and why.
Before/after comparison names improvements, unchanged dimensions, declines, and limitations.
The artist manually marks completion and schedules a focused delayed reconstruction.
self_review_questions: Does every major decision trace back to the brief?
Which structural correction produced the largest downstream improvement?
Which tutor suggestion did I reject or qualify, and why?
Do front, turned, and expression views retain the identity card?
Are controlled asymmetry and perspective clearly separated?
Does the value design explain the same light in every view?
What limitation remains, and what exact delayed exercise will address it?
practice_prompt: Create the complete capstone sheet: brief/identity specification, front construction, three-quarter construction, expression/asymmetry variation, two-value lighting pass, and corrected final comparison. Preserve the initial evidence and manually decide completion.
